text:
alex: Heads up — seeing intermittent retransmits and ~0.2-0.6% packet loss between gpu-pool nodes in us-west-2 during model load bursts. Tail latency for small gen jobs spikes from 40ms -> 220ms. Looks like something in the overlay path.
maya: which nodes/pods? time window?
alex: last 30m, affected pairs: gpu-node-13 <-> gpu-node-19, gpu-node-21 -> gpu-node-13. Happened in bursts every ~7-12s. tcpdump shows dup acks and immediate retransmits. snippet:
```
14:32:11.123456 IP gpu-node-13.49212 > gpu-node-19.443: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12478, ack 54321, win 64240
14:32:11.123789 IP gpu-node-19.443 > gpu-node-13.49212: Flags [R.], seq 54321, ack 12478
14:32:11.124010 IP gpu-node-13.49212 > gpu-node-19.443: Flags [.], seq 12478:12478, ack 54322
14:32:11.124200 IP gpu-node-13 > gpu-node-19: TCP DUP ACK
```
sam: could be NIC offload + overlay coalescing issue (GRO/GSO/TCP segmentation). Any ethtool -k on the interfaces? also check qdisc drops (`tc -s qdisc show dev eth0`).
alex: ran ethtool -k eth0 on gpu-node-13, here's key parts:
```
$ ethtool -k eth0
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
scatter-gather: on
tcp-segmentation-offload: on
generic-segmentation-offload: on
generic-receive-offload: on
large-receive-offload: off
```
and dmesg has repeated mlx5e reset notices around the bursts:
```
mlx5_core: Port 1 link down. Resetting core
mlx5_core: Firmware event: HW error, resetting
```
nate: recent kernel/driver changes in us-west? I think we pushed mlx5 driver update in the 00:15 deploy earlier.
maya: if it's offload+overlay, disabling GRO/GSO on the VF or veth could make the issue disappear at cost of CPU. Can we test on one canary node?
sam: quick test: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off` on the node and re-run the workload. also try `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_moderate_rcvbuf=0`? (not sure) — but measuring CPU impact is needed.
alex: did `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off` on gpu-node-19 at 14:35. Immediate drop in retransmits in tcpdump. tail latency back to ~45ms. CPU for kubelet/containers on that node jumped ~15%.
maya: good signal. So likely NIC fw/driver interacting badly with overlay reassembly. We should avoid fleet-wide flipping until vendor/driver root cause.
nate: propose: (1) mark gpu-node-19 as canary, keep GRO off, (2) open vendor ticket with mlx5 logs/firmware dumps, (3) schedule rolling restart of other gpu nodes with GRO off if more nodes show issue, (4) consider kernel rollback if vendor says regression.
alex: filed vendor ticket (ticket# MLX-8921). collected `mlx5_core` trace and `ethtool -S eth0` dumps and attached to ticket.
deploy-bot: Rolling update started for nodes: gpu-node-20,gpu-node-21 (strategy=canary, max_unavailable=1)
maya: capture perf/cpu delta and perf counters for a few hours, tag cost impact for infra team — disabling offloads increases inference CPU cycles which increases cost per-token.
alex: agreed — tracking cost delta in the ticket and our incident board. For now we keep GRO off on the canary and watch 6h.
sam: also let's capture eBPF LPM/flow samples + tcp retransmit histogram so we can pattern-match bursts vs qdisc drops.
alex: will add eBPF probe job and share graphs. thanks all.
